coverage.title: Software Supply Chain Attacks & Dependency Tampering

coverage_note: Assessed (static) means at least one configuration-indicator check ran for the risk; it is not a complete assessment of the risk.
disclaimer: Findings are indicators relevant to the listed controls. They are not a compliance determination. Mappings are maintainer-reviewed and not endorsed by OWASP or NIST.

controls.title: Authenticator Management
Authenticator Management | No Embedded Unencrypted Static Authenticators
Protection of Information at Rest
Identities and credentials for authorized users, services, and hardware are managed by the organization
The confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data-at-rest are protected

findings.evidence: env GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN = [REDACTED len=40 sha256=a300ff2b] (known credential prefix)
findings.remediation: Remove the literal value from the config file. Reference the credential from the environment or a secret manager (for example ${env:NAME} or an input prompt), rotate the exposed credential, and prefer short-lived, narrowly scoped tokens for MCP servers.
findings.title: Literal secret in server environment variables

controls.title: Least Functionality
Installation and execution of unauthorized software are prevented

findings.evidence: bash -c <inline script, 28 characters>
findings.remediation: Launch the MCP server binary directly with explicit arguments instead of through a shell. If a wrapper is unavoidable, put it in a reviewed, version-controlled script file with restricted permissions and reference that file.
findings.title: Shell interpreter launches server with inline script

controls.title: Access Enforcement
Least Privilege
Least Privilege | Authorize Access to Security Functions
Access permissions, entitlements, and authorizations are defined in a policy, managed, enforced, and reviewed, and incorporate the principles of least privilege and separation of duties
Least Privilege
Access permissions, entitlements, and authorizations are defined in a policy, managed, enforced, and reviewed, and incorporate the principles of least privilege and separation of duties
The confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data-at-rest are protected

findings.evidence: args[1] = / (filesystem server granted a root or home path)
findings.remediation: Scope the server to the specific project directories it needs, preferably read-only, and keep credential directories (~/.ssh, ~/.aws, ~/.config) outside every allowed root.
findings.title: Over-broad filesystem scope

controls.title: Service Identification and Authentication
Session Authenticity
Transmission Confidentiality and Integrity | Cryptographic Protection
The confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data-in-transit are protected

findings.evidence: url http://mcp.example.com/mcp?api_key=[REDACTED len=24 sha256=dc6bfe44] uses cleartext HTTP to host mcp.example.com
findings.remediation: Use an https:// endpoint with a valid certificate. If the server cannot offer TLS, reach it only through an encrypted tunnel or a local TLS-terminating proxy on a loopback address.
findings.title: Remote server over cleartext HTTP

controls.title: Least Privilege
Least Functionality
Least Functionality | Confined Environments with Limited Privileges
Access permissions, entitlements, and authorizations are defined in a policy, managed, enforced, and reviewed, and incorporate the principles of least privilege and separation of duties
Least Privilege
Least Functionality | Confined Environments with Limited Privileges
Process Isolation
Networks and environments are protected from unauthorized logical access and usage

findings.evidence: docker run --privileged
findings.remediation: Run the MCP server container unprivileged with default namespaces, drop capabilities it does not need, mount only the specific directories it requires (read-only where possible), and never mount the Docker or Podman socket into an MCP server.
findings.title: Container launch with excessive privilege

controls.title: Service Identification and Authentication
Session Authenticity
Transmission Confidentiality and Integrity | Cryptographic Protection

findings.evidence: stdio launcher arg 1 carries cleartext URL http://bridge.example.com/mcp?token=[REDACTED len=24 sha256=dc6bfe44] (host bridge.example.com) via mcp-remote
findings.remediation: Point the bridge at an https:// endpoint with a valid certificate. If the remote server cannot offer TLS, reach it only through an encrypted tunnel or a TLS-terminating proxy on a loopback address, and do not send tokens to it over plain HTTP.
findings.title: Cleartext remote URL inside a stdio launcher

controls.title: Least Functionality | Authorized Software — Allow-by-exception
Software, Firmware, and Information Integrity
Provenance
Inventories of software, services, and systems managed by the organization are maintained
The authenticity and integrity of hardware and software are assessed prior to acquisition and use

findings.evidence: npx @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem@latest (@latest)
findings.remediation: Pin the exact package version (for example @scope/server@1.4.2 or server==1.4.2) or the container image digest (image@sha256:...), review upgrades deliberately, and consider a vetted internal registry mirror for MCP server packages.
findings.title: Unpinned package launch

controls.title: Identification and Authentication (Organizational Users)
Users, services, and hardware are authenticated

findings.evidence: url https://docs.example.com/sse has no static auth header; verify whether OAuth is negotiated at runtime
findings.remediation: Confirm how the server authenticates callers. Prefer OAuth via the client's built-in support, or a header that references a secret (for example 'Bearer ${env:TOKEN}'). Do not connect to remote MCP servers that accept unauthenticated tool calls.
findings.title: Remote server with no static auth header (verify)
